#3523. Decoding Kate Middleton’s “Tourdrobe” for Her Trip to India

When Kate Middleton stepped out on the green carpet at the Earthshot Awards ceremony in Mumbai this week, it was “an absolute princess moment,” says British designer Amanda Wakeley.

“Catherine has really come into her own. She has found her stride and a new confidence, and you see that in this dazzling but also practical ‘tourdrobe,’’’ Wakeley, who has previously dressed the Princess of Wales and used to dress Princess Diana, tells Vanity Fair.

It has been 10 years since Princess Kate last visited India. Her fashion choices are more sophisticated now than on her visit in 2016, and the speech she delivered at the Earthshot Prize ceremony on November 17 shows a new confidence. With her elevated look, there’s no trace of High Street labels. Kate’s flared floral dresses and the wedge shoes she used to love (but the late Queen Elizabeth apparently disliked) have been replaced by Manolo Blahnik pumps, couture power suits, and clothes by some of her favorite designers, such as Emilia Wickstead.

Prince William and Princess Kate attend The Earthshot Prize Awards Ceremony at the Jio World Convention Centre on November 17, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

Kate’s decision to wear a striking vermilion dress made from handwoven silk by New Delhi–based designer Mahima Mahajan to the Earthshot Prize ceremony spoke volumes. The eye-catching dress, which she paired with a burgundy Prada velvet clutch, was chosen after Kate had selected a special suite of emeralds from the royal gem collection. The green stones on the dress perfectly matched her jewels, which served as an homage to both Queen Elizabeth II and India, as the green of the Indian flag represents growth and prosperity.

The dazzling stones known as the “emerald tassel suite” were worn frequently by the late Queen Elizabeth II, and while Kate has previously worn the earrings, this marked the first time she wore the set. The effect was dramatic.

“Never has Catherine looked more like a queen in waiting,” Wakeley says of the look.

Wearing the suite ensured that Kate, who has free rein of the royal jewels, looked more regal than ever. “What was fascinating was seeing Catherine wear these incredible family heirlooms along with more relaxed collections from some of her favorite modern jewelry designers like Kiki McDonough and Astley Clarke,” remarks Wakeley.

Kate’s carefully curated wardrobe for the trip wasn’t just about power dressing—it was also about showing she can be sustainable as well as on trend.

“It was good to see Catherine making a proper nod to sustainability by rewearing her Roksanda dress,” Wakeley notes. “It’s clear a lot of thought has gone into her outfit choices. Her wardrobe has to be practical, and her clothes have to work harder than most people consider for their clothing; she needs weight in the hem of the floaty dresses. She has learned lessons the hard way. She is often seen bending down, talking to children, so she’s conscious of how low a neckline is, how short a skirt is.”

Princess Kate visits the Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital, on November 18, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

For her visit to Mumbai’s Nowrosjee Wadia Maternity Hospital on November 18, Catherine chose a striking red tailored Emilia Wickstead skirt suit with Manolo Blahnik pumps. On November 16, she opted for a pistachio blazer by designer Veronica Beard, paired with white Alexander McQueen trousers and pearl-buckled Camilla Elphick flats, a relaxed and accessible look for when she picked up a cricket bat.

Princess Kate plays cricket on November 16, 2026 in Mumbai, India.

As Princess of Wales, Catherine is often compared to Princess Diana. “The main difference is Diana was a fashion icon. Catherine has become a style icon,” Wakeley says. “There’s a big difference. Diana played into the fashion of the day and was finding her style. During the time she resigned from public life, she worked out her style DNA. Catherine has had to do that on the job. Very wisely, she has worked out her style and doesn’t get too impacted by fashion and trends. She goes for what she likes. What works for her rather than trends. She really knows now what works for her.”

The holidays are a great time to be around family and celebrate their company, but they are always more difficult when you’ve just lost a loved one. Breaking Bad cast member RJ Mitte died on October 12, 2026, at the age of 34 by suicide. The loss is still fresh for his mother and sister, and they took some time to publicly pay tribute to him on Thanksgiving.

Mitte famously played the son of Walter White, Walter Jr., on the hit AMC show for five seasons along with a host of other roles. He was also a disability rights activist who spoke out about living with cerebral palsy since he was a toddler. Check out how his mother, Dyna Mitte, paid homage to her late son on Thursday:

A post shared by Dyna Mitte (@dyna_banana)

Mitte’s mom shared a photo of herself with RJ Mitte and his sister Lacianne Carriere. She wrote that she’s “missing” him on Thanksgiving, but she “made all [his] favorites”. RJ’s sister also took to her Instagram account to share a throwback photo with the late actor. Here it is:

RJ’s younger sister expressed that she’s “thankful for the time” she had with her brother, and is really feeling his absence on the first holiday she and her family are spending without him. About a month ago, Carriere took to the platform to share a long tribute to RJ, calling him her “everything” and “other half”. It’s a particularly huge loss for his closest relatives.

Mitte’s body was found by his mother on the morning of October 12 in his home in Brownville, Texas. His official cause of death was ruled a suicide the same day. His mother said she had offered and suggested her son go to therapy in the three months before his passing, but he said he was “OK” and “handling it” (via Today).

RJ’s mother said she would have dragged him “screaming and yelling” to seek professional help if she knew what would happen. His mom also said she thinks the suicide might have been a “spur of the moment” decision because he didn’t leave a note behind.

RJ Mitte had spent time with Breaking Bad co-star Luis Moncada shortly before his passing, and she expressed that the actor had been “struggling”. His mother said RJ had “already signed deals on several new movies”, was working on a book and was starting a food truck before his death. Mitte had also popped the question to his longtime girlfriend Kennedy Suarez a year ago.

The actor started on Breaking Bad at the age of 14 and continued to have a main role on the beloved series throughout its mind-blowing run. Through the role, he brought his experiences with cerebral palsy to television without it ever being central to his character.

Bryan Cranston spoke to the actor’s death by saying he was in “deep despair” at the news and recalled RJ Mitte playing the role of Walter Jr. with “such joy and enthusiasm” in an Instagram post. Aaron Paul also paid tribute to the actor at the time of his death on Instagram, saying he’s “so sorry you were hurting my friend. I wish we knew.” As his family, friends and fans continue to mourn the loss of RJ Mitte, we send our condolences.

If you or someone you know is in crisis, we urge you to call or text 988 to reach the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline or chat live at 988lifeline.org.

Brightness is the U8QG’s main advantage, with the manufacturer estimating up to 5,000 nits of peak brightness, while PCMag measured around 3,200 nits when reviewing the 65-inch model. Its Mini-LED local dimming also produces deep blacks, although some light bloom can appear around bright objects on dark backgrounds. Audio-wise, its built-in 4.1.2-channel system, which includes surround channels, a subwoofer, and upward-firing speakers, gives movies more scale than typical TV speakers, though a separate sound system can still offer clearer separation and a broader soundstage.

The U8QG also has plenty to offer gamers using a current-generation console or a capable gaming PC. It supports refresh rates up to 165Hz, variable refresh rate, and AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, with a measured 4.3 milliseconds of input lag at 1080p and 120Hz and 10.1 milliseconds at 4K and 60Hz. Those results should make controls feel responsive, even during fast-paced games. There’s also a side-mounted USB-C port that accepts DisplayPort video, while Google TV handles streaming alongside Apple AirPlay and Google Cast. The biggest inconvenience is the limited selection of three HDMI ports, since a console, soundbar, and streaming device would occupy all of them.

So, I’d expect a director to move mountains in order to get her on their film. It turns out Pugh had balls of steel even before she earned her A-list status. When she was just 22, she was faced with the ultimate Sophie’s Choice of movie roles.

If you were to ask me what two Florence Pugh movies turned her from a burgeoning talent into a one of my favorite actors alive, I’d say it was the one-two punch of her portraying Dani in Midsommar and playing Amy March in Little Women back in 2019. As it happens, those are the same two films that she almost had to pick between. Pugh shared what it took to land both, recently, and I had no idea.

I knew in my gut that I had to do both. And, I knew that if I let one of them go, I would regret that decision for the rest of my life. I called both directors with a big ball of nerves in my stomach because I really wasn’t at the stage of my career where I should be calling a director and telling them that they need to reschedule their shoot, but I did.

This, ladies and gentleman is yet another reason why Florence Pugh is the major name she is. She clearly understood at the time that she had stumbled onto two incredible parts, and she didn't want to choose, despite others telling her she must. With that in mind, she pushed aside any fears and decided to simply ask for what she wanted. Here’s what happened next, per her interview with Elle:

I remember just telling myself like, ‘This is really hard. This is going to require for you to be very brave, but you need to do this because if you don’t you’ll regret not trying.’ And I did, and they made it work. So, I’m grateful for that.

Pugh ended up shooting Midsommar first with writer/director Ari Aster, which proved to be a taxing shoot for the actress. It was all worth it because the A24 film has since become known as one of the best horror movies of all time, with Dani’s May Queen and the Bear also becoming a popular Halloween costume, too. Pugh later also got a Midsommar tattoo to immortalize the movie on her body.

Right after she made Midsommar in Hungary, Pugh ventured to Massachusetts to make Little Women with writer/director Greta Gerwig alongside a cast including Timothée Chalamet, Saoirse Ronan, Emma Watson, Laura Dern and Meryl Streep. Whew, what a list! Little Women went on to give Pugh her first (and still only) Oscar nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Oh, and it also changed how we think about Amy March being a villain in the literary classic, probably forever.

While it feels like the absolute correct order for Pugh to have shot the films, she has spoken about getting depressed after coming home from the leftover Midsommar feelings she had “shelved” when making the joyful book adaptation about sisters.

Pugh's story goes to show, sometimes you just need to ask for what you want, and maybe you’ll get it! It’s particularly a good anecdote for people who might think they need to “earn” the right to request something, when that’s not always the case! And thank goodness she did, because her roles in Midsommar and Little Women are and will always be all-timers for her.

#3518. Beats' Newest Over-Ear Headphones Are Down to a Record-Low $249 for Black Friday

While you can find plenty of deals on older headphone models during Black Friday sales, it’s rare to see a record-low price and a nearly 30% discount on newer, highly rated models from top brands. That’s exactly why this deal on the critically praised Beats 360 headphones should be on your radar. They’re now down to $249 (originally $349.99) in Amazon’s early Black Friday sale.

With a design that looks like the love child of the AirPods Max and the Beats Studio Pro, these have an adjustable telescoping frame and a unique modular design that lets you mix and match ear pad colors. The color-swapping bundle isn’t currently on sale, but it’s reassuring to know you can replace the ear pads as they wear out.

They’re controlled by two buttons on each earcup and powered by a dedicated Beats chip, with support for both Android devices and iPhones. You can switch noise modes and, on an iPhone, activate features like Personalized Spatial Audio in Settings. They last up to 32 hours with ANC on, which is longer than both the more expensive Sony WH-1000XM6 and AirPods Max 2.

According to Beats, the 360 offer up to 1.75 times the noise cancellation of the Beats Studio Pro. PCMag’s review, which gave the headphones an “Excellent” rating, was impressed by how well they blocked out everything from plane engine noise to café chatter. The noise cancellation falls short of pricier models, and PCMag found the Sony WH-1000XM4C slightly better in that respect.

The PCMag review says the headphones deliver “nice, deep bass, reasonably crisp highs, and a more neutral tuning than you might expect for a pair of Beats headphones.” If you’re after long battery life, rich audio, and plush earcups you can swap for a pop of color, $249 is a great price for the Beats 360 headphones.

#3517. 6 Upcoming Steam Games To Wishlist For Life After GTA 6

With December right around the corner, a very busy year for video games is coming to a close. And while some players might be spending that last month working through Grand Theft Auto 6, there are still a few new PC games coming out before the calendar changes to 2027.

For Wishlister this week, we've rounded up six upcoming Steam games coming out in December that you won’t want to sleep on. It’s a wide-ranging list, spanning cozy games starring mice exploring Sweden to a horror game about sentient instruments. Whether you want a relaxing wind-down after GTA 6 or something more stressful, there are plenty of upcoming games to toss on your wishlist.

Following up on 2025’s hit A Game About Digging a Hole, publisher Rokaplay Select is capitalizing on its success with a multiplayer spinoff. A Game About Digging a Hole Together features all the hole-digging satisfaction of the original game, but with support for up to four players to work together at once.

Do you miss your Rock Band glory days? Well, you’ll soon be able to relive them in Stage Tour. RedOctane Games’ debut rhythm game is a Rock Band revival in everything but name. You’ll be able to jam along to a soundtrack of licensed songs using plastic instruments. Olivia Rodrigo, Radiohead, Metallica, and more will appear in the stacked playlist.

Poised to be December’s biggest WTF game, Don’t Fret sure has one head-turning premise. It’s a horror game set inside of a school overrun with musical monsters. It looks like a mod for a Silent Hill game that replaces Pyramid Head with Cassette Head. It’s both creepy and colorful, setting the stage for a very unique horror game.

A throwback to the golden age of mascot-driven platformers, Waltz and Jam looks like a revival of a classic series that doesn’t actually exist. You’ll play as a ghost and its dog as they journey through the afterlife. With levels inspired by the seven deadly sins, Waltz and Jam looks to breathe some delightfully creative ideas into one of gaming’s foundational genres.

Co-op enthusiasts are getting a cozy little treat this December with Hela: Of Mice and Magic. Inspired by the sights of Northern Sweden, you and your friends will play as tiny mice exploring a big world. The pastoral adventure might be the perfect destressor after a few weeks of crime sprees.

The survival crafting genre is about to get much smaller. Trollheim: Gnomes is a co-op game that lets up to eight players control gnomes looking for shelter in a vast forest. Inspired by Nordic folklore, the early access game looks to capture some of the same magic that has made Valheim a smash hit.

#3516. Blade Runner 2099 Proves The Saga Does One Thing Better Than Any Other Sci-Fi Franchise

Continuing the legacy of two of the greatest sci-fi movies ever made is a big enough challenge. Doing so on the small screen adds an extra element of difficulty. Incredibly, "Blade Runner 2099" has overcome the odds to deliver yet another intoxicating excursion into the techno-industrial urban decay-scape so magically realized back in 1982's "Blade Runner" and so faithfully recreated in 2017's "Blade Runner 2049." As such, the Blade Runner franchise is now surely the most consistent on-screen sci-fi saga ever made. (Setting aside sci-fi sagas that are directed by the same person the whole time, like James Cameron's "Avatar.")

It's hard to imagine, but "Blade Runner" had a tiny VFX budget. Yet director Ridley Scott and his production team managed to create one of the most believable and immersive worlds in cinema history. The famous "Hades" opening shot immediately plunges you into a future post-ecological collapse, in which technology seems to have almost grown on the wreckage of a fallen world like moss on fallen trees. The debris of society is adorned with neon and machinery, creating an environment in which past and future collide. "Blade Runner" might have been buried at the box office by "E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial," but it was an absolutely enthralling sci-fi adventure that came to define the genre.

As such, when Denis Villeneuve managed to both emulate the feel of Scott's classic and push the production design in new directions with "Blade Runner 2049," it was nothing short of a miracle. The "Dune" director's take on the world first introduced to audiences in 1982 was immediately familiar as the same one in which Harrison Ford's Rick Deckard did battle with Rutger Hauer's Roy Batty and his band of rogue Replicants. Yet it also felt appropriately evolved for the three-decade time jump. Surely "Blade Runner 2099" couldn't pull off the same trick — especially across eight episodes? Well, it has.

/Film's Bill Bria has hailed "Blade Runner 2099" as the best sci-fi show in years, and it's hard to disagree based solely on the production design. From the moment the show begins, we're immersed in the same world to which Ridley Scott introduced us back in 1982. In fact, "2099" recreates the "Hades" sequence so faithfully you'd think you were watching the original. It's a clever move, too. As the camera slow-zooms on the Tyrell Corporation building and evokes the tone and feel of Scott's film, it establishes "2099" as very much belonging to the "Blade Runner" legacy. But we soon discover that this is not Rick Deckard's future.

80 years after Harrison Ford's Blade Runner absconded with Rachael (Sean Young), Replicants have now overthrown their human masters to become the dominant race. It's a major change that refreshes the franchise and helps make it more relevant than it's ever been at a time when the looming AI garbage future has prompted widespread talk of machines taking our jobs.

As such, it's more important than ever to maintain a tone and design language that's consistent with what came before, so as to reassure fans of the saga that this isn't some sort of wholesale reinvention of the franchise they love, but an evolution that plays out in the same world. "Blade Runner 2099" impressively pulls that off with its opening scene, and it only gets better from there.

When it comes to the world of "Blade Runner," fans know the deal: Retro futurism and cyberpunk aesthetics meet noirish expressionism in a technological nightmare future. Many franchises have tried to emulate the aesthetic to varying degrees of success, but there is only one "Blade Runner." As Christopher Nolan once told the Directors Guild of America while discussing Ridley Scott's film, it conjures "that feeling that there was this whole world outside the frame of the scene. You really felt there were things going on outside of those rooms where you've seen the film take place."

"Blade Runner 2099" has somehow managed to make every one of its scenes feel like they belong in that same world. With that in mind, it's truly remarkable how consistent the Blade Runner universe has remained across almost a half-century's worth of projects, each of which has been separated by many years. Even the best sci-fi franchises struggle to pull off what is, admittedly, an almost impossible trick.

The "Terminator" movies have never been able to recapture the intoxicating, doom-laden sci-fi slasher tone that made the first two films so memorable. The "Alien" franchise, meanwhile, has made a point of switching up its style and tone with each successive film — though more recent projects have tried to evoke the feeling of the 1979 original. "Blade Runner" films, however, all feel part of a cohesive whole that gives the entire saga this uncanny sense of existing in a real alternate timeline somewhere — as if we're witnessing an epic, decades-spanning dream play out in the mind of a dying Replicant. Regardless of how you feel about "2099" as a whole, its visual and tonal achievements simply can't be denied.

"Blade Runner 2099" Season 1 is now streaming on Prime Video.

Black Friday deals start showing up long before Black Friday actually arrives, and it's easy to shop most sales online without ever having to set foot in a store. But if you are willing to go early, stand in line, and navigate the crowds, you may be able to get some free stuff for your effort. Here are the freebies on offer this Black Friday.

The first 100 shoppers in line at Target on Black Friday will receive a gift card worth $25, $50, or $100, and one shopper at every store will get a $1,000 gift card. Stores open at 6 a.m., and tickets redeemable for free gift cards will be handed out starting approximately an hour before. Shoppers must exchange their tickets for their gift card within the first hour after doors open.

The first 200 shoppers at every Kohl's store on Black Friday will get a voucher for Kohl's Cash worth $5 to $100. Doors open at 5 a.m. If you show up on Saturday, Nov. 28 instead, you're eligible for a Sephora at Kohl's coupon (also worth $5 to $100).

If you're a MyLowe's Rewards member and you show up early on Black Friday, you could get one of several free buckets filled with products and coupons. JCPenney is running scheduled giveaways in stores throughout the day on Black Friday, so you could get free products even if you aren't there when doors open. If you line up at 5 a.m., you will get a peel-away card that is good for $10 off, $50 off, or $500 off your purchase, as well as a free Harry Potter mini snow globe. Academy Sports is distributing bonus cards worth $20, $50, or $100 to the first 100 customers in line on Black Friday between 5 a.m. and 6 a.m. CT. Prize amounts will be randomly awarded among entrants. Academy Sports has locations across more than 20 states.

Best Buy's Black Friday promo isn't strictly free, but members of the My Best Buy rewards program (including the free tier) can purchase a $100 gift card for $60. There is a limit of one per person while supplies last, and cards can be used immediately, so you can take advantage of sales.

The first 30 shoppers at Golf Galaxy locations on Black Friday are eligible for instant prizes, including products, gift cards, and in-store services. One person per location will win a swag bag worth more than $500. Doors open at 7 a.m.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

#3514. Prince William Reportedly Wants to Strip Prince Harry of His Titles

Prince William is reportedly actively considering a plan for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”

The plan was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”

By implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

They may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could issue letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

In October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”

Kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”

#3513. The Cliff Booth Movie Brings Back Two Key Characters From Once Upon A Time In Hollywood

This article contains spoilers for "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth."

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is not a direct sequel to "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood," as we knew from Quentin Tarantino handing over the director's chair to David Fincher. But still, you had to wonder if any other familiar faces would pop up in this new mis-adventure.

Part of the appeal of returning to the world of "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" is that the movie ended by changing history. Thanks to the actions of Cliff, actress Sharon Tate (Margot Robbie) is not murdered by the Manson family. How does the entertainment world and Los Angeles change by 1977, when "Cliff Booth" takes place, because of that ripple effect? Tarantino wrote the script for "Cliff Booth," and if any filmmaker is equipped to dig into the nitty-gritty of such a change in Hollywood history, down to the most obscure B-pictures and forgotten TV, it's him.

Now, the major supporting cast of "Cliff Booth" is totally different. Cliff's best friend, actor Rick Dalton (Leonardo DiCaprio) — for whom Cliff worked as a stunt double and driver back in 1969 — does not appear due to DiCaprio declining a cameo appearance. The movie mentions a few times that Rick moved to Australia and is currently starring in a popular TV show there, "Dingo Dan." Tarantino has also devised some stories about what happened to Rick after that fateful August 9, 1969 night.

But a few of the fictionalized Hollywood characters return for brief cameos: Margot Robbie as Sharon Tate, Timothy Olyphant as actor James Stacy, and even Nicholas Hammond as TV director Sam Wanamaker (in a smaller role).

One of the Quentin Tarantino Easter eggs in "The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is a commercial for Red Apple Cigarettes, a fictional brand that appears in other Tarantino movies. The actress in the commercial is Sharon Tate, with Cliff smiling at her and likely recalling how he saved her life. "Once Upon A Time In Hollywood" cast Sharon Tate in an angelic light, down to giving her the happy ending that reality didn't. But revisiting her in greater depth, like what became of her marriage to Roman Polanski or how her acting career played out, would risk adding a dash of salt to that sweet ending.

The alternate history of Sharon Tate in "Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" earned obvious comparisons to Tarantino's "Inglourious Basterds," which also starred Brad Pitt (as Lieutenant Aldo Raine, leader of the Nazi-killing Basterds). In that movie, Adolf Hitler (Martin Wutke) dies at the hands of Jewish soldiers instead of by suicide. That leads into Timothy Olyphant's "Cliff Booth" cameo, which feels self-recursively inspired by "Basterds."

"Once Upon a Time in Hollywood" mixes real Hollywood history with pastiche. Much of the first half sees Dalton filming a guest spot on a TV Western, "Lancer," which was a real show back in the late '60s. Olyphant appears as the real-life star of "Lancer," James Stacy, and the episode is directed by Nicholas Hammond's Sam Wanamaker, the real director of the "Lancer" pilot episode. "Cliff Booth" gives us another glimpse of Stacy and Wanamaker working in this alternate timeline's television industry.

Since 1969, Cliff Booth has become a fixer: someone who (violently) solves problems for Hollywood fixtures wrapped up with criminals. Fictional TV star Charlie Winters (Scott Caan) becomes one of his clients. The movie includes a newsreel style montage, narrated by Quentin Tarantino himself, recounting Winters' rise to TV stardom.

One of Winters' shows is "Enemy Territory," about a U.S. pilot trapped behind enemy lines in Europe during World War 2. The narrator describes the show as "'The Fugitive' with Nazis, but 'The Fugitive' with Nazis is a fun idea." (I'd watch it!) We see Winters shooting a scene where his character threatens a Gestapo officer into helping him rescue a captured American general. The officer is played by none other than Timothy-Olyphant-as-James-Stacy, doing a broad German accent with a high pitch reminiscent of Christoph Waltz's Colonel Hans Landa from "Inglourious Basterds."

Sam Wanamaker is directing the scene. Stacy's performance is being criticized as "a smidge cavalier" — so Winters puts a live round in the prop gun with which his character is threatening the Gestapo officer. Stacy, sure enough, begins acting like a man whose life is being balanced on the edge of a trigger.

Casting Olyphant as James Stacy was a nod to how his real most famous roles are on Western TV shows — namely, Sheriff Seth Bullock in HBO's "Deadwood" and Deputy U.S. Marshal Raylan Givens in the Kentucky-set neo-Western "Justified." But Olyphant has got range beyond playing cowboys, and his comic energy in his "Cliff Booth" cameo is just more evidence of that.

"The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth" is playing in theaters, with a Netflix release date of December 23, 2026.

Perez's Lucia has been a big topic of discussion over the past week, as couples joke that their partner is cheating on them with her. She didn't have anything to say about that, as it seems like she's just now catching her breath and sharing gratitude on Instagram to the fans that helped make the game's release bigger than any show on the 2026 TV schedule:

I guess I shouldn't be surprised that Manni Perez looks a lot like Lucia, as Grand Theft Auto does like to model its characters after the voice actors who play them. Still, even well-known celebrities can look a little different in the game, whereas Perez looks like she could star in a future movie about Jason and Lucia. It would be awesome if she were considered for the role if there are discussions!

William Shatner Clarifies His Stance On Grand Theft Auto VI After Backlash

No joke, I would guess there are as many people listening to her voice in the game as there are who saw some of the biggest releases on the 2026 movie schedule. It's good to see her be so humble about it all, and she has nothing but gratitude to everyone enjoying the game.

Lucia and Jason are a hot topic after the release of Grand Theft Auto VI, as they buck the usual trend of what we've seen from previous games in this franchise. Previous entries haven't had existing relationships for players to maintain, and I wouldn't say the protagonists were necessarily anyone the player felt compelled to root for.

Lucia is also the first female protagonist of Grand Theft Auto, as players can opt to swap between the two in order to complete missions. While there was some initial backlash to the game making such a radical change, it appears that the people are more in support of the decision than against it.

Grand Theft Auto VI is available to purchase right now, and a great buy for those looking for something to spend the rest of the year obsessed with. I've spent a couple of hours in the game just listening to the various radio stations in my car, and can't wait to see what other stuff unlocks the longer I play it!

#3511. 10 of the Best 'GTA 6' Cheat Codes, and How to Use Them

Cheat codes have long been a part of the Grand Theft Auto video game franchise, and the tradition continues with GTA 6. Not only does GTA 6 support cheats, but it also has a menu that lists all of them as well as instructions for unlocking them. However, you cannot fire up the game and start using cheats from the beginning. In fact, it requires quite a bit of work on your part. Here's how to unlock cheat codes in GTA 6, how to see the list of cheats, as well as the 10 best cheat codes in GTA 6.

Gone are the good old days when you could fire up GTA, enable god mode, unlimited ammo, no reload, spawn a jetpack, and run around the entire city destroying things at will. In GTA 6, you'll need to complete the main story to unlock the ability to use cheat codes. On top of that, you'll have to complete challenges of various difficulty levels to access specific cheat codes. Some of these cheats unlock the moment you finish the main story. Others, however, are quite challenging or time-consuming. For instance, unlimited reload requires you to win 25 gold medals at shooting ranges.

Once you complete the main story in GTA 6, just go to in-game settings, and you'll see a new Cheats tab. This lists all 61 cheats and how to unlock them. You'll see the actual button combo for each cheat right after you complete the unlock requirement.

Unfortunately, there are some serious gameplay ramifications to using cheat codes in GTA 6. For starters, you can't save the game once you input even one cheat code. That's why it's best to save before you start using cheats, to avoid losing progress. Using cheat codes will also disable trophies and achievements in GTA 6.

To start using cheat codes in GTA 6, you'll have to get your character to pull up the smartphone by pressing the up arrow on the D-Pad. Then, hold L1+R1, and press the cheat's key combination on the D-Pad.

While there are a lot of cheat codes in GTA 6, these are 10 of the best, listed with the right key combination, and the condition to unlock them:

This cheat unlocks the moment you complete the main story in GTA 6. To use it, press up, right, down, left, up, left, down, right.

You unlock this cheat code after losing a three-star wanted level 25 times. The key combination is left, down, right, down, up, down, up.

Lose a three-star wanted level 50 times to unlock this cheat. The key combination is left, down, right, down, up, right, up.

This cheat unlocks the moment you wrap up the main story. Press this to unlock: down, up, up, down, up, down, up, down, up, right.

This is the third cheat that unlocks when you finish the main story. When you shoot or punch/kick characters, this cheat will launch them in the air. The key combination is: down, up, left, right, down, down, up, down

If you win 25 silver medals at shooting ranges, you can unlock infinite ammo in GTA 6. The key combination is: down, up, right, down, left, left, up, down, down, down.

To stop needing reloads, you need to win 25 gold medals at shooting ranges in GTA 6. The key combination is: down, up, right, down, left, left, up, down, down, up.

If you complete 100 workouts during your GTA 6 playthrough, you'll unlock the cheat that lets you instantly obtain body armor. Press this key combination to make it work: down, up, left, up, up, up, up, up, down, down.

This GTA 6 cheat allows you to change the weather at any time, and it unlocks when you finish the main story. Press this key combination to toggle it: down, right, up, down, right, up, right.

#3510. The Return of Malin Akerman and Brittany Snow’s Twisted ‘Hunting Wives’ Love Story

In 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

The plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

“I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”

“I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” says showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”

The result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.)

Hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter says, “and eventually seduced.”

Cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she says, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”

Cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

“The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter says, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”

The twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a New York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

Cutter says she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain plan of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”

The second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

“Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter says, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”

#3509. Forza Horizon 6 Still Beats GTA 6 in One Key Way

There's driving and there's racing, and only one game excels at both

Rockstar Games is justifiably proud of everything it put into Grand Theft Auto 6, and one technical detail the studio has taken the time to highlight is the game's vehicle physics simulation. According to Ben Lyons, Rockstar's technical director for physics, some of the team started building and racing cars after finishing Grand Theft Auto 5, even winning in their class at the Nürbrugring 24 hours.

"This taught us a huge amount about how to modify, design, and set up real cars to go fast and what happens to them when things go wrong, like bursting tires and crashing," Lyons told Polygon in a statement. (As if to underline the point, Lyons' LinkedIn profile pic shows him proudly holding up a blown racecar tire in a pit garage.) "We also took the same approach with rally-racing dirt bikes — it’s important to us to understand the difference between racing on two and four wheels and on- versus off-road so we can give our players as convincing authentic experience as we can," he said. "For this game, we completely rewrote the vehicle simulation for every vehicle type so we could add more detail and realism, as well as authenticity and believability, to the game."

Knowing how detail-obsessed Rockstar's developers are, and how seemingly limitless their resources were, I wondered if GTA 6's handling physics would be able to hold their own against the best the racing game genre has to offer​​​​​​​. My interest was doubly piqued when Polygon's reviewer Giovanni Colantonio told me there was a ton of racing in the game, both in the form of organized events on racing circuits and impromptu street races. Could GTA 6 secretly be a great racing game, along with everything else?

The answer is: no, not really. The cars are great to drive, and the races can be fun, but the design and technology of GTA 6 are fundamentally not set up for racing, and it shows.

As a benchmark to measure GTA 6 against, I chose Forza Horizon 6. It wouldn't be right to compare Rockstar's everything-game to the most realistic circuit-racing sims, but an open-world racing game that has entertaining, accessible, and credible driving physics, with a degree of depth, seemed like fair game.

GTA 6's racing options are hardly minor. Street-racing leagues unlock in chapter 3, but you can roll up to any circuit and start racing, or log some time trial laps, from the very beginning. A racing career is even a viable way to make money in the game. If you have enough cash for the entry fee and to rent a competitive ride (or you could just steal one), the payouts for top-three placements represent a decent profit.

As a driving — as opposed to racing — game, there are a number of things that GTA 6 actually does better than Forza. For starters, there's the clearest fruit of Lyons' racing experience: the damage modelling. It's not as astounding as the soft-body physics in BeamNG.drive, but GTA 6 does have extremely detailed and reactive damage that meaningfully affects car handling and performance as well as smashing and peeling away body panels. Big plus.

I've already written about GTA 6's genius use of the PS5 DualSense controllers' adaptive triggers to allow for easy, relaxed driving at cruising speeds when exploring or just driving from place to place. That's something I wish Forza Horizon could have. And while Forza Horizon 6's Japan has more outright beautiful scenery than GTA 6's Leonida, the incredible richness and detail of Rockstar's game makes it an equal or greater pleasure to explore. The roads are much busier with traffic, all of which seems to be driven by reactive (if somewhat chaotic) humans rather than Forza's silent automatons. Also — not an insignificant detail when it comes to the cruising experience — the radio stations are much better.

For sheer driving pleasure, I wouldn't put GTA 6 ahead of Forza, but it's not far behind. The rolling gait of its soft-suspension civilian rides makes them fun (if not easy) to chuck around, and drifts and tail-wagging burnouts are easy and satisfying to pull off. You get a good sense of the surface you're driving on when off-roading, and the world around you has much more credible and reactive physics than it does in Forza, including things like mud and street furniture (which, in Forza, all appears to be made from either balsa wood or the hardest substance known to man).

But anywhere where you care to examine the games' racing chops, Forza wins out. GTA 6's car customization has great cosmetic options, but the performance upgrades are rudimentary compared to Forza's. Forza has a manual transmission option, which, if you want to use it, grants much finer control over, and connection with, the car.

When you're actually racing, the gulf opens up. GTA's racing AI is in the spirit of the whole game's AI: it's chaotic, violent, and random. Races are tough to win because anything can happen, not because the racers are actually competitive. They're knockabout, almost slapstick affairs in which there's seldom any sign of anyone trying to follow a racing line. I've been in GTA 6 races with five or six cars driving abreast down the straight and then sideswiping each other on the corners. It's madness.

In the end, GTA 6's most profound failing as a racing game might also be its subtlest. It's the camera. It's not just that there's no in-car or first-person view (unless you're looking at your phone, which I do not recommend). Even the chase cameras, which look much like those of Forza Horizon 6, are just not as well tuned for racing. I'm not quite sure why — I think it has something to do with elevation and field of view, as well as the way the camera moves with the car as it turns — but it's much harder to pick and hold a line through a corner in GTA 6. You feel as though you're pushing your car around the circuit from above rather than sitting in it.

This effect isn't helped by the undefined track design, the handling model's tendency toward understeer, and the lack of audio and tactile feedback about where the edge of the car's grip is. Specifically when racing, GTA 6 feels woolly, where Forza is razor sharp.

This is a fundamentally unfair exercise; GTA 6 isn't a racing game, and it isn't really trying to be. As a driving game, it's hugely pleasurable, with a distinctive character and an amazing world to explore. The races are a fun diversion. But if you compare them to a true racer like Forza Horizon 6, you get a very swift and clear lesson in design intention. It doesn't matter how much money or detail went into GTA 6, or how good its physics model is; compared to something that was built for purpose, it ends up looking sloppy.

Playground, you have two months to put this in Forza Horizon 6 on PS5

#3508. The Hunting Wives Season 2 Review: The Steamy Netflix Drama Hits The Mark Again

This review contains discussions of addiction.

I deeply respect when a show or movie knows what it is. Let's use the original run of "Gossip Girl" as an example. This delightfully dishy show started out as a series about teenagers behaving badly in New York City and became a flat-out soap opera — in the best way — where characters marry princes, make deals with God after near-fatal car accidents, and sell each other for hotels. My point is that "Gossip Girl" made a choice, at a certain point, to steer into the proverbial skid and just be as absurd and insane as possible, because the show knew it was high camp, not high art.

I would put "The Hunting Wives" in the same category, and I mean that as a distinct compliment. Created by Rebecca Cutter and adapted from May Cobb's book of the same name, "The Hunting Wives" premiered in the summer of 2025 and introduced Netflix audiences to Brittany Snow's Sophie O'Neil, who moves from Cambridge, Massachusetts to the heartland of Texas when her husband Graham (Evan Jonigkeit) gets a lucrative job working for oil tycoon and political hopeful Jed Banks (Dermot Mulroney). When Sophie — who's in recovery as an alcoholic after killing a pedestrian while intoxicated behind the wheel back in Cambridge — encounters Jed's wife Margo Banks (Malin Åkerman), she finds herself drawn into Margo's social circle and drawn to Margo herself, and the two start a torrid affair as teenagers start turning up dead in the seemingly idyllic community of Maple Brook.

"The Hunting Wives" is back for Season 2, and it's steamier, dishier, sillier, and sexier than ever. If you liked how hot and nuts the first season was, you'll be happy to hear Cutter has turned the dial up to 11.

After the Season 1 cliffhanger ending where Sophie accidentally kills Margo's beloved but law-breaking brother Kyle (Michael Aaron Milligan), there's a lot to deal with in Season 2 of "The Hunting Wives." Jed is continuing his run for governor, but both he and Graham are furious that their wives cuckolded them; Sophie and Margo are estranged over the fact that Sophie figures out, in the final episode, that Margo is responsible for the death of the teenaged Abby Jackson (Madison Wolfe). (Margo isn't one of 2025's best TV villains for nothin'.) Despite this, the two end up in bed together pretty promptly in Season 2, and they're just as hot together as ever; if you loved all of the steamy scenes in "The Hunting Wives" Season 1, rest assured that there's plenty for you to enjoy here.

Across the board, Season 2 of "The Hunting Wives" takes everything you loved about Season 1 and delivers it in spades. Guns are blazing, kisses are passionate and steamy, and the interpersonal drama is as wild as ever; Brittany Snow and Malin Åkerman are excellent, once again, as two women locked in a love affair that constantly threatens to derail both of their lives. Even as the stakes get sillier and higher, Snow and Åkerman treat every moment that they're on-screen, separately or together, with the utmost seriousness. Remember what Michael Caine did in "A Muppet Christmas Carol?" That's basically what these two powerhouses actresses are doing in "The Hunting Wives," but with considerably more nudity ... and it rocks. The second outing of "The Hunting Wives" forces Margo and Sophie the most heightened situations imaginable, but thanks to Snow and Åkerman's performances, you believe that they're hopelessly in love.

My biggest critique of a show as fundamentally unserious as "The Hunting Wives" is that its lack of gravity can brush up against legitimately serious in-universe issues. By that, I mean Sophie's drinking. Sophie killed someone in a drunk driving accident before this show's story began, and even though the show does make you root for her relationship with Margo, it also seems to want to make a larger point that Sophie is addicted to Margo ... especially because Margo typically pours Sophie a drink when they're together. To call this message muddled would be ... generous.

With all that said, I would certainly hope that people dealing with addiction aren't looking to a show like "The Hunting Wives" for a realistic portrayal of that issue. This is also a show where, by the end of Season 2, the body count is in the double digits — and I actually mean that in two senses, because there's a litany of dead bodies and a ton of new romantic trysts by the time the season finale's credits roll.

Honestly, across the last few episodes of Season 2 — critics received the entire eight-episode season — the number of corpses that pile up gets so out of control that the deaths stopped being shocking and started feeling routine. (Without getting into major spoilers, Brad breaks bad in a big way, and it honestly grows tiresome pretty quickly.) I still want to be clear, though: "The Hunting Wives" isn't prestige television, and it knows it. It doesn't always need to be impeccable or even make sense. It's fun, and it fulfills that qualification pretty beautifully.

Dale Dickey, who's finally getting more recognition after years as a supporting small-screen player thanks to her outstanding supporting turn in the perfect 2026 comedy "Widow's Bay," is a perfect new addition to Season 2 of "The Hunting Wives" as Zelda Moffitt, the formidable head of a Texan motorcycle gang who has a connection to Margo's past. Soap opera star Kim Matula is excellent as Nadia Kelly, a reality TV producer with an ulterior motive, and John Stamos and Cam Gigandet have small but impactful roles as talent scout Chase Brylan and Zelda's son "Gentle John" Moffitt, respectively.

As much as he made my skin crawl, though, I have to give full credit to "The Wilds" alum Alex Fitzalan, who appears as the conniving campaign manager Lincoln Trout. As Jed's new right-hand man — with an emphasis on the word right — Fitzalan's Lincoln is disgusting, reprehensible, and compulsively watchable. I suspect he'll play a pretty large role in Season 3, and as horrifying as he is writ large, I sort of can't wait to see more.

Speaking of Season 3, the sophomore season of "The Hunting Wives" leaves us with such a good cliffhanger — which did genuinely surprise me after the back half of the season got just a tiny bit bogged down with murder after murder after murder — that I cannot wait until the planned third season is available to watch. "The Hunting Wives" is one of the most patently ridiculous shows airing right now, and that's not a bad thing at all; in fact, it's exactly what makes it such an incredibly fun ride from start to finish.

"The Hunting Wives" is streaming on Netflix now.

#3507. The Home Depot Is Giving Away Free Milwaukee, DeWalt, and Makita Cordless Power Tools for Black Friday

Jeff Somers is a freelancer who has been writing about writing, books, personal finance, and home maintenance since 2012.

Jeff has published nine novels and more than 70 short stories; his story Ringing the Changes was selected for inclusion in The Best American Mystery Stories 2006. In 2018, Jeff published the book Writing Without Rules: How to Write & Sell a Novel Without Guidelines, Experts, or (Occasionally) Pants. He holds a bachelor’s degree in English and previously worked in medical publishing as a production editor.

When not writing, Jeff spends his free time fixing up his old house. He has tackled a wide range of DIY projects, including remodeling a bathroom entirely on his own in two weeks, and building a roof deck that hasn't fallen down yet. You can find him on Bluesky.

As anyone who has ever shopped at The Home Depot (or any hardware store) knows, power tools are expensive. That’s why Black Friday at The Home Depot is so important: It’s the perfect opportunity to get the tools you’ve been wanting at some pretty steep discounts. And the best deals even give you a free tool if you purchase a starter kit from one of the major tool brands (Ryobi, DeWalt, Makita, or Milwaukee).

Here’s how this year's “buy one, get one” (BOGO) deal works: Pick out a starter kit from one of the brands, add it to your cart, and you’ll be presented with a list of available tools you can add (they’ll be marked “FREE,” so you can’t get confused). When you go to check out, the price of the tool will be listed as “SAVINGS.”

Here are the starter kits you can choose from:

Ryobi ONE+ 18V Starter Kit (includes one 4.0Ah and one 2.0Ah battery and charger). Cost: $99.

DeWalt 20V Max Starter Kit (includes 6.0Ah and 4.0Ah batteries and charger). Cost: $199.

Makita 18V LXT Starter Pack (includes two 5.0Ah batteries and a rapid charger). Cost: $199.

Milwaukee M18 FUEL Combo Kit (includes a brushless, cordless hammer drill and an impact driver). Cost: $399.

Note that the Ryobi, DeWalt, and Milwaukee offers include 14 free tools to choose from, while the Makita offer only includes 8. Also, note that while the Ryobi starter kit is your cheapest option for a free tool, the batteries included are weaker. The DeWalt or Makita batteries cost more, but offer more power and flexibility.

Some of the deals go beyond just getting a freebie. For example, if you choose the DeWalt Starter Kit for $199, you can get an Atomic 20V Max impact wrench that normally costs $239 for free, which is a significant savings even if you already have batteries and a charger and don’t really need those items (plus, you can never have too many batteries).

The Home Depot is also offering deep discounts on just about everything in the store. Some of the most notable tool deals include:

50% off this DeWalt Cordless Brushless Oscillating Multi Tool, including battery and charger

33% off this Ryobi Combo Kit, an incredible deal for a circular saw, reciprocating saw, and a power drill/driver plus two batteries and a charger; the batteries are small, but this is a great deal on a starter kit.

42% off this Combo Kit from Milwaukee, including a Packout toolbox, a hammer drill, an impact driver, a grinder, and a reciprocating saw, plus two batteries and a charger—a massive deal for anyone who needs to tool up rapidly.

45% off this Brushless Cordless Impact Wrench Kit from Ryobi, which includes a battery and charger.

That only scratches the surface—if you’ve ever needed anything from Home Depot, Black Friday is the day to run out and get it.

Of course, Black Friday can be a little chaotic, so here are a few tips to maximize your savings and experience:

Check online and in-store. Some deals are in-store only, and some items (especially BOGO tools) may not be available at your nearest location—make sure you enter your ZIP code when you’re checking out to ensure you won’t have any problems.

Consider whether you need more batteries and chargers. Depending on your existing collection of batteries and chargers, buying more to get the discount may or may not make sense.

There's no price matching or rain checks. Remember that the store won’t honor price-matching or offer rain checks on Black Friday items.

Cyber Monday will have deals, too. More deals will be rolled out on Cyber Monday (November 30), which may include items you want but don’t see on sale for Black Friday. But keep in mind that Black Friday prices probably won’t go any lower—so snap up what you need as soon as you can.

Sign up for text alerts to save a little more. Home Depot offers a $5 coupon (off a purchase of $50 or more) when you sign up for email or text alerts, which you may be able to apply to your Black Friday purchase for a little extra savings.

Home Depot isn’t the only store offering free tool giveaways:

Like Home Depot, Lowes is offering BOGO tools with the purchase of starter kits from major tool brands.

Tractor Supply Co. has a wide range of BOGO tool offers during its Black Friday Event.

If you’re looking for outdoor equipment, note that Bass Pro Shops and Cabela’s aren’t offering a BOGO deal this year, but the first 250 customers at each physical store will receive a free “mystery promo card” valued between $10 and $500. If you’re going to go for this, plan to line up early—250 cards are going to go fast.

The best early deals on tools right now are at Home Depot, where you can get up to 65% off on select Milwaukee tools, 50% off on DeWalt tools, and 30% off on Ryobi tools. They also have several offers for over 50% off on hand tools..

Home Depot and Lowe’s often compete with each other for seasonal sales, so it’s always a good idea to check both sites before buying. Right now, Home Depot has the best deals on DeWalt and Milwaukee cordless tool sets, but Lowe’s has a better deal on Craftsman hand tool sets.

The best prices of the year on tools are during the holidays in November and December. This is because of the holiday shopping push, as well as making space for new tools that come out in the spring. The second-best time to buy tools is in May and June during Father’s Day sales.

In 2019, Danny Boyle, who was originally named the director for the James Bond film that eventually became No Time to Die, suggested Robert Pattinson as the man to take over as the next person to play Bond. Now, seven years later, that prediction has come true, as Pattinson was officially named the next 007 last week. Boyle isn’t done making suggestions, however, but now he’s switched to who should play the villain: Jack O’Connell.

In an interview on Alchemy with Anthony Mason, while promoting his new movie Ink, Mason brought up Boyle’s prognostication, and Boyle took it one step further, saying:

But we have an actor in [Ink], Jack O'Connell, [who] would have been a great Bond, as well.  And now I can see that in all this talk, they're talking about Jack O'Connell as a possible villain. They have that thing you want to watch them.  And it's impossible to quantify what it is. Otherwise, we’d all buy it for ourselves.

O’Connell was one of the (many) actors who were rumored to be in the running for Bond 26 before Amazon MGM and director Denis Villeneuve ultimately decided to go with Pattinson, and I think his take on O’Connell as the villain is also an inspired idea as well. Along with who could be the next “Bond Girl,” the next Bond Villain is another big casting chip that still needs to fall soon before filming kicks off, hopefully in 2027.

O’Connell isn’t the only name being bandied about to play James Bond’s next villain. Another actor who has worked with Boyle before, Cillian Murphy, has been a popular choice among fans. Barry Keoghan, who worked with Murphy on the 2026 movie schedule in Peaky Blinders: The Immortal Man (which was headed up by Bond 26 writer Steven Knight), is also a top pick. Idris Elba, whom many hoped (including me) could be the next Bond, though even he admitted he’s too old for the role now, is also a common name thrown out there (and honestly, maybe my pick).

Last week, after the Pattinson announcement, Brad Pitt even tossed his own name into the ring for the role. Now that would be an interesting choice! The latest rumors also point to Tom Hardy as the next villain, which would set up an interesting dynamic between the current Batman (Pattinson) and a former Batman villain (Hardy played Bane in The Dark Knight Rises).

There are still quite a few casting announcements for Bond 26 to look forward to, like M, Q, and Moneypenny, in addition to the villain, maybe a henchman or two, and, of course, the next Bond Girl. Oh, and who could possibly be in line to do the next Bond theme? It’s an exciting time to be a Bond fan. Meanwhile, Ink will be available to watch with a Netflix subscription on January 8th, after a short stint in theaters starting on December 11.

Hugh Scott is the Syndication Editor for CinemaBlend. Before CinemaBlend, he was the managing editor for Suggest.com and Gossipcop.com, covering celebrity news and debunking false gossip. #3505. 84 Years Later, Casablanca's Best Line Is Still The Most Romantic Quote In Movie History

If you're not familiar with "Casablanca," I have to assume that you're from some sort of alien planet, have been in a coma for decades, or are a newborn baby. Directed by Michael Curtiz and written by Julius J. Epstein, Philip G. Epstein, and Howard Koch (whose script adapts the play "Everybody Comes to Rick's" by Murray Burnett and Joan Alison), "Casablanca" centers around the taciturn bar owner Rick Blaine (the incomparable Humphrey Bogart), an American ex-pat living in the titular city in Morocco (which was still a colony of France at the time, as the film is set in December 1941). As Rick accepts refugees and ex-pats of all stripes (and has an anti-Axis and anti-Nazi past of his own), he also quietly ensures paperwork to people looking to escape the Nazi regime.

That's when Ingrid Bergman's Ilsa Lund walks into Rick's particular gin joint, to sloppily paraphrase one of his best quotes (and we'll circle back to that). After Ilsa and Rick had a beautiful love affair in occupied Paris and planned to escape together, Ilsa simply vanished, which gave us the bitter, cynical, and lovelorn Rick we see living in Casablanca. Not only is Ilsa back, but she needs a favor: Her husband Victor Laszlo (Paul Henreid), whom she believed was dead when she romanced Rick in Paris, needs papers to evade the Nazis hunting him so that the couple can run away to Portugal (which is unoccupied). Not only does Rick give Ilsa the papers that she and Victor need, he gives up the woman he loves so that she and Victor can live their lives safely. "Casablanca" is a sweeping story of righteous protest against fascism, lost love, and sacrifice ... and "Here's looking at you, kid" is one of its most memorable lines.

"Casablanca" is, admittedly, stacked from top to bottom with memorable quotes (more on that shortly), but "Here's looking at you, kid" feels like it transcends the very film it came from. There are probably people out there who don't even know that this sweet nothing came from this 1942 classic (and I'd like anyone who doesn't to sit their butt down and watch all of "Casablanca" right now), yet the fact of the matter is that "Here's looking at you, kid" has stood the test of time and remains one of the most immortal lines in movie history.

So, why is that? Rick says this line to Ilsa throughout "Casablanca," and we see him utter it during flashbacks to the couple's happier times in Paris and right before he puts her on the plane with Victor that will take her to Portugal safely. It's simple but unbelievably meaningful. Before understanding why Ilsa suddenly left Paris, Rick was furious that she vanished from his life. When she reveals that she only left because Victor was alive, sick, and needed her help after he escaped from a concentration camp, his heart softens, and he's able to forgive her for the heartbreak she caused. Rick loves Ilsa, and there's no denying that Ilsa loves Rick, but she's in love with Victor — and the film smartly doesn't villainize Victor, making him a genuinely decent guy who simply wants to escape enemy forces and live peacefully with his wife after years of torment. "Here's looking at you, kid" is Rick's expression of love for Ilsa, and him saying it right as he puts her on a plane that will take her away forever is both heartbreaking and romantic.
