#3376. 8 Live-Action Transformers Designs That Are 10/10 Perfect

Across the entire live-action Transformers franchise, there are just some designs that will never be beaten. Without a doubt, Michael Bay changed the game in 2007 with the start of his live-action series, breathing new life into the entire Transformers franchise as a whole. Part of that includes some of the raddest live-action robots to ever be seen on the big-screen.

Since the 80s and the original animated series, characters like Optimus Prime, Bumblebee, and Megatron have had very distinct looks both in animation and as physical toys. As a result, translating those iconic depictions to live-action was always going to be one of the biggest hurdles to getting audiences on board. That said, very few live-action Transformers designs look bad, and a select few have certainly achieved GOAT-status.

Keeping that in mind, here are 8 of the most perfect, 10/10 live-action Transformers designs we absolutely love, based on pure cool factor, unique appearances that just work, and/or excellent live-action translations.

Without question, Devastator is one of the most ambitious and intimidating designs in the live-action Transformers franchise, largely due to the sheer scale of the massive Decepticon. Formed from six different Constructicons (just like in the original animated series), Devastator is a huge Combiner who debuted in 2009's Revenge of the Fallen, deployed by Megatron in Egypt to uncover the giant Star Harvester hidden within the Great Pyramid of Giza.

Rather than combining from construction vehicles that are all the same green-and-purple color, each piece of Devastator is mismatched with various colors, along with a gaping maw of a mouth and multiple eyes. As such, the industrial monster that is Devastator has one of the scariest and most intimidating live-action Decepticon designs, despite his limited screen time in the Transformers franchise.

Also debuting in Revenge of the Fallen, Sideswipe is one of the sleekest Autobots in the live-action movies. Transforming into a silver Chevrolet Corvette Stingray, Sideswipe's most notable design feature in his robot form is two car wheels positioned as his feet like roller skates, allowing him to move across a battlefield with more fluid motion than most of his fellow Autobots. He also has large blades on his arms, making his distinct fighting style even more of a unique threat to the Decepticons.

Debuting in 2014's Age of Extinction, Crosshairs' chosen vehicle form is notably a later-model Chevrolet Corvette Stingray, having a shared vehicle form with Sideswipe in the earlier Transformers films, with a green color scheme rather than silver. However, what makes Crosshairs so awesome is that he arguably has one of the most stylish robot forms in the live-action Transformers franchise, having an effortlessly cool coat-like configuration of vehicle parts that very much adds to his gunslinger personality/aesthetic. Likewise, Crosshairs' dual pistols cement his role as an Autobot survivor/combat specialist.

Debuting in 2011's Dark of the Moon, Decepticon Shockwave has one of the coolest and most powerful designs in the live-action movies. Featuring a single eye just like his counterpart in the original animated series, the emotionless Shockwave on the big-screen commands his Driller pet, a huge Cybertronian beast made up of several devastatingly massive mechanical tentacles, making him one of the most formidable Decepticons in the entire franchise. While he doesn't receive nearly enough screen time in Dark of the Moon, Shockwave is easily one of the biggest and scariest threats.

Debuting in the first live-action Transformers movie, Michael Bay's Megatron design is more original compared to his more traditional, G1 look. However, the unique design eventually became iconic in its own right and is certainly one of the most intimidating and fearsome-looking versions of the Decepticon leader across the franchise.

Having an incredibly angular and pointed appearance with jagged edges, sharp teeth, and clawed hands, Megatron is the epitome of a deadly weapon brought to life. Capable of turning into both a brutal tank and alien jet in the live-action movies, the Bayverse Megatron is a prime example of a design that has major cool factor points, despite its more original appearance.

As a major caveat to this list, it has to be noted that the brief Cybertron flashbacks in 2018's Bumblebee feature some of the coolest G1-inspired live-action designs, quick as they are. While it seems unfair to the entire live-action franchise to simply list all the bots seen in just a couple of minutes of screen time, personal bias compels me to at least include Soundwave.

Unlike the version seen in 2011's Dark of the Moon, the version of Soundwave seen in Bumblebee embraces everything that made his original G1 so awesome, including his monotone vocoder voice, blue-and-gray color scheme with yellow accents and red eyes, shoulder cannon, and chest compartment to launch his various cassette minions like Ravage and Laserbeak. A perfect combination of classic G1 appearance with more modern detailing, Soundwave's design in 2018's Bumblebee is easily one of the coolest and most satisfying when it comes to the live-action Decepticons.

Now we get to Bumblebee himself, who's easily one of the most important bots in the entire Bayverse and beyond as Optimus Prime's loyal lieutenant who's also best friends with crucial human characters like Shia LaBeouf's Sam Witwicky and Hailee Steinfeld's Charlie Watson.

Bumblebee has gone through several different live-action designs with his classic yellow-and-black color scheme, starting with his epic Camaro vehicle forms that redefined the look of the character for a new generation of Transformers fans, complete with car-door "wings" on his back and a face shield with insectoid-like eyes to help add to his namesake. However, the classic Autobot's appearance in his 2018 solo movie arguably provides the best balance between G1 authenticity with a more classic 1967 Volkswagen Beetle vehicle form, while still keeping with the robot design established in the earlier Bayverse movies.

With slightly more rounded proportions thanks to his classic vehicle form, Bumblebee looks so good in his spin-off. However, that isn't to say he's ever looked bad in earlier movies or the Transformers films that followed with his truly awesome Camaro forms. Also, his expressive face does wonders for the character, who more often than not uses radio frequencies to speak to make up for his damaged voice. He's a true "heart of the franchise" character if ever there was one.

It shouldn't come as a huge surprise that Optimus Prime ranks at the top of this list. As the noble leader of the Autobots, Optimus has arguably received the most attention of any character in the entire live-action Transformers franchise, and for good reason. While he's had many different forms and designs over the years with varying levels of authenticity to the classic G1 look, you really can't go wrong with the OG live-action that debuted with Michael Bay's first film back in 2007.

Optimus Prime's live-action debut was a major cinematic achievement, translating his classic semi-truck appearance into a mechanical form that felt both practical and natural in "real life." Featuring red flames and accents on a blue frame, Optimus' OG form still holds classic features like his iconic face shield and distinct head design, while still having a more complex and modernized form to best convey how a truck could indeed transform its parts into a massive robot body in live-action.

Not every Optimus Prime form has been universally loved (The Last Knight's wasn't great), and more recent versions like the Optimus seen in Bumblebee and Rise of the Beasts have embraced G1 aesthetics even further, which has been cool to see. Nevertheless, the Bayverse's OG design is arguably still the best for live-action Optimus Prime, and the most perfect 10/10 design for the entire Transformers franchise overall. Without such a solid look and design for Transformers' most central character and hero, I sincerely doubt the franchise would have done as well as it has.

#3374. The 10 Greatest Rock Albums of the '60s, Ranked

The '60s was a hugely important era for rock music – perhaps the most important decade for the progression of the genre. Folk and protest influences were abundant, and the British Invasion was globalizing the genre. The counterculture was in full swing, bringing a psychedelic edge to rock and roll. The world was in a state of constant transformation, and the music of the decade mirrored this relentless change. Musicians began to experiment like they never had before, pushing the boundaries of what was possible – and what was socially acceptable. There was so much variety and innovation during this time that picking the top ten rock albums of the 1960s may seem like an impossible task. And, yet, here they are.

The second album from chaotic British rock band Cream definitely made an impact. An incredible amount of creativity and experimentation was packed into these eleven songs (clocking in at a mere 33 minutes.) Both of the singles released ahead of this album — “Strange Brew” and “Sunshine of Your Love” — charted in the UK, and the latter made it to number five in the US. Disraeli Gears bridged the gap between their earlier blues rock sound with the psychedelic tint they later took on. Perhaps “earlier” and “later” are the wrong words – the band dissolved after only three years together due to irreconcilable differences between bassist Jack Bruce and live-wire drummer Ginger Baker.

Willy and The Poor Boys by Creedence Clearwater Revival is about as far as you can get from the psychedelic rock wave taking over the UK and the US. This album is straight up Americana swamp-rock. The narrative storytelling and the focus on the American middle class make this album a stand-out and a fan favorite. The record was initially supposed to be a concept album, written and recorded from the perspective of fictional jug band Willy and The Poor Boys. While they didn’t end up following through with this idea, some of the texture remained – the story of the jug band that never was is expressed through the popular track “Down on the Corner.”

Led Zeppelin II is widely considered to be the band's heaviest album. Their music style was evolving as the '60s slipped into the '70s – they were reshaping traditional American blues music into something with much more firepower. This album included three covers of Chicago-based blues songs and six original tracks. It was written while Led Zeppelin was on tour, recorded in myriad studios and cities (and even on Jimmy Page’s houseboat!) This constant relocation added to the chaotic feel of the album. But despite the constant motion, Zeppelin II comes together as a cohesive record, featuring dynamic shifts in volume and tone, driving guitar, and musical (rather than lyrical) hooks.

Electric Ladyland is the third and final album from the Jimi Hendrix Experience. The record initially confounded critics – they weren’t sure whether to love or hate the trippy, immersive, funky acid rock album Hendrix had created. It was an unprecedented piece of work, so some confusion is understandable. Nowadays, the record is regarded as one of the greatest albums in rock and roll. Hendrix referred to these songs as "sound paintings,” which is abundantly evident in the album. Each track is layered and ambient, drawing the listener deep into a bottomless well of sound. And lest we forget – this album also includes Hendrix’s legendary reinterpretation of Bob Dylan’s “All Along the Watchtower.”

Jim Morrison and The Doors were a darker voice in the 1960s counterculture. On their self-titled debut album, the group mixes poetry, blues, psychedelia, and experimentation to create an incredibly important record. This record was developed through live performances, mostly at LA’s iconic venue Whiskey a Go Go. They released their single “Light My Fire” ahead of the album, which quickly got the public interested in their music. The Doors had an inconceivable impact on the bands that came after them, across a wide array of genres. Alternative rock and punk would not be what they are today without the music of The Doors.

What's a rock and roll list without The Rolling Stones? Their eighth studio album Let It Bleed is a return to their earlier blues, gospel, and hard rock sound. The record was also heavily inspired by American roots music and the overwhelming feeling of disillusionment much of the Western world experienced throughout the 1960s. Let It Bleed includes some of their biggest hits to date, such as “Gimme Shelter” and “You Can’t Always Get What You Want.” Throughout the writing and recording of this album, the band was in a time of intense turmoil. Founding member and guitarist Brian Jones was slipping deeper into addiction and failing to show up for rehearsals, resulting in his termination from the group. He tragically passed away a few weeks later. He was replaced by Mick Taylor, and both musicians appear on the album. Keith Richards had to pick up a lot of the slack in the string section, which permanently altered the band’s sound. The release of Let It Bleed ushered in the band’s most successful period.

Tommy by The Who took six months to write and record — an unusually long period for bands at this time. This extended interval was well worth it, producing an iconic and unprecedented concept album. It would be impossible to rush the complex storytelling, theatricality, and groundbreaking scale of the record. Tommy, written by guitarist Pete Townshend, was the first album to be labeled a "rock opera". Townshend was inspired by Indian spiritual practices. The album follows the fictional Tommy Walker through his life, which is plagued by murder, abuse, and drugs. Tommy overcomes these myriad hardships to eventually become a messiah figure and spiritual leader. Tommy is widely considered to be The Who’s breakout album.

Highway 61 Revisited is Bob Dylan’s sixth studio album. In this body of work, we see Dylan depart further from folk music, incorporating an increasing number of rock musicians in the studio. This album is in many ways a continuation of his 1965 record Bringing It All Back Home. Dylan’s poetic lyrics capture the political and cultural unrest of America in the midst of the Vietnam War. His lyrics are steeped in clever allegory and impressionism, buoyed by a relentless blues-rock drive. With each album release, Dylan’s energy and rebellion grows.

The Velvet Underground & Nico was greatly underappreciated during the time of its release. It is the band’s debut album, a collaboration with German model and singer Nico, a partnership that was carefully engineered by artist Andy Warhol. The record tackled unconventional and controversial subject matter like drugs and sadomasochism, which shocked the public — it was banned from many radio stations and record stores. The Velvet Underground’s avant-garde, abrasive sound did well in New York City’s underground scene, but pretty much nowhere else. They were well before their time, setting the stage for punk, alternative, and psychedelic rock. Many consider it to be the original art rock record. Today, it is finally appreciated for the masterpiece that it truly is.

The Beatles’ Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band is a landmark psychedelic rock album – perhaps the most important body of work to come from the 1960s. This record was a huge moment in popular culture and helped to define the Summer of Love. It is an early example of a concept album, wildly innovative in every aspect of creation and production. The album is based upon a fictional band conceptualized by Paul McCartney and includes a vast array of whimsical and unusual influences, including vaudeville and circus music. This incredible album set the stage for prog rock and countless other genres, changing the face of rock and popular music forever.

#3373. iPad Air vs iPad Pro: Which should you buy?

Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well.

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

The iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

The iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

The iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

For most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

#3368. This iPad Is a Lifehacker 'Gift of the Year' Award Winner, and It's $50 Off During Black Friday

If you're shopping for an iPad this holiday season, you might be a bit intimidated by Apple's price tags. The iPad mini starts at $599; the base iPad Air is $749; and the entry-level iPad Pro is a whopping $1,199. Most of Apple's iPad line certainly lives up to its expensive reputation.

That's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

The iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

The iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

Apple says this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

The only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for users who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee plans to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes, Apple participates in Black Friday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

Yes, Apple participates in Cyber Monday, though you may want to compare their sales with other retailers like Best Buy, Amazon, and Walmart. So far, the best Black Friday sale on an Apple product is the M5 MacBook Air on sale for $200 off, the lowest price since the price hike this summer.

#3367. Things 3.25 update brings new touch features to the MacBook Pro

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

Swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

#3365. All 2 DC TV Shows & Movies Releasing On HBO Max In December 2026

DC fans can get ready for a new movie and the latest season of a long-running series to arrive on HBO Max in December to end 2026 in style. What a ride this year has been for DC Studios, who ends it in a much different place than when it started. After all, 2025 was the height of James Gunn's DCU.

Superman's release finally allowed DC to have the highest-grossing superhero movie of the year in a long time, beating three Marvel Cinematic Universe films. However, with Supergirl becoming a major box office bomb and Clayface not turning into a hit like other 2026 horror movies, sentiment regarding the DCU soured, and as Paramount closed its deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, everything changed.

Gunn and Peter Safran are out as DC Studios co-CEOs, with former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham now set to update the plan for DC's characters moving forward. Amid this period of uncertainty, there are no new DCU projects set to drop in December. The shared universe will return next year with Gunn's Superman movie sequel, Man of Tomorrow, and shows like Mister Miracle and The People v. Gorilla Grodd.

While the DCU has ended its slate of releases for 2026, there are other Elseworlds franchises, which exist outside the shared universe's canon, with projects that superhero fans can enjoy in December. Both of them are animated, including a movie and a TV show, though they are completely different in tone. These are the two DC movies and TV shows coming to HBO Max in December:

Batman: Knightfall Part 1 is the first film in a new animated trilogy that adapts one of the Dark Knight's most iconic stories from DC Comics. This is the classic story that saw Bane break Batman both emotionally and physically, which has been adapted in a Batman movie before. After all, one of the best directors of all time, Christopher Nolan, used elements of the Knightfall arc for his final adventure with the DC hero, The Dark Knight Rises. However, the Batman movie was not all that accurate to the comic book storyline, which is where Batman: Knightfall Part 1 comes in.

The animated Knightfall trilogy's plan is to be as close to the comics as it can be, with key characters like Azrael, Nightwing, Robin, and more being part of this new movie franchise. In Batman: Knightfall Part 1, Bane breaks Batman's Rogues Gallery out of Arkham Asylum, creating a gauntlet of villains for the Dark Knight to face until he is exhausted, which is when Bane proceeds to break Batman himself. This is the DC release on HBO Max in December for older viewers, as the Batman movie is R-rated, allowing the Dark Knight's fights with villains to be visceral.

Batman: Knightfall Part 1's cast comes with major stars, as Star Trek and Marvel Cinematic Universe actor Anson Mount voices Bruce Wayne, while Spider-Man: Brand New Day's Scorpion star, Michael Mando, gives life to one of the most haunting versions of Bane to date. Batman: Knightfall Part 1 will be released on HBO Max on December 7, just in time for viewers to get ready for its sequel, Batman: Knightfall – Part 2: Knightquest, which releases on digital on December 15.

Teen Titans Go! is simply the longest-running DC series of all time, which is an impressive feat, and its latest batch of episodes, season 9, releases on HBO Max on December 20. The Teen Titans make up one of DC's best teams, perhaps second only to the Justice League, with charismatic characters and a nice balance of powers. Teen Titans Go! also stars the same cast of the original 2003 Teen Titans animated series, with Scott Menville (Robin), Hynden Walch (Starfire), Tara Strong (Raven), Greg Cipes (Beast Boy), and Khary Payton (Cyborg).

Teen Titans Go! Season 9 will also become available on Hulu on December 28.

Teen Titans Go! is fun for the whole family, making for a great introduction to the wider DC universe for kids, while also being written for adults in a sense. There are a lot of references and jokes that older viewers will be able to spot, with the show's humor being suited for viewers of all ages. Season 9 features a wide range of DC characters besides the Teen Titans, with Harley Quinn, Black Canary, The Penguin, Swamp Thing, Hawkman, Lex Luthor, Superman, The Joker, Darkseid, and more appearing. These are all the DC movies and TV shows being released on HBO Max in December 2026.

The three movies released by Paramount and Warner Bros. following their merger under the Skydance Corporation have delivered uneven results at the box office. However, the studio's most recent release appears to be losing momentum after three weeks in theaters. The animated movie is facing fresh competition from Disney's new big-budget film​​​​​​​ Hexed this week, after competing with Laika's critically acclaimed Wildwood​​​​​​​. While the W.B. film wasn't as expensive to produce as Hexed — the Disney fantasy movie has a reported budget of $200 million — it wasn't as critically acclaimed as Wildwood either.

Directed by Travis Knight, Wildwood continued Laika's exquisite streak of releasing acclaimed stop-motion gems; the new movie holds a "Certified Fresh" 97% score on the aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes and has grossed around $80 million worldwide so far, against a reported budget of $100 million. Four worlds and four completely different ideas of what a good life looks like. This is where you belong, what it would ask of you, and what you would get back in return.

You belong somewhere old enough that the mountains have names and somebody can still tell you who gave them. Middle-earth is for people who think the right thing is worth doing even when it will not be finished in their lifetime.

You want the sea, a crew, and absolutely nobody telling you where you are allowed to go. The Grand Line is the world for people whose main ambition in life is finding out what is over there.

You would rather be feared and useful than liked and useless. The Continent is a world where the monsters are the straightforward part of the job and the people are where it all gets complicated.

You want the myths to be real and loose in the actual world, and you want to find out at about thirteen that you were never anywhere near as ordinary as everybody kept telling you.

We're talking, of course, about The Cat in the Hat, the second major adaptation of Dr. Seuss' famed children's book. The film features Bill Hader as the voice of the titular character, along with Xochitl Gomez and Matt Berry in supporting roles. Its Rotten Tomatoes consensus reads, "A high-energy sprint through the world imagined by Dr. Seuss, The Cat in the Hat's eagerness to please has some charm but could have benefitted from smaller stakes and a less frantic pace."

The movie has so far grossed a little under $75 million at the global box office, and comes on the heels of fellow W.B. movies such as Lee Cronin's The Mummy, Mortal Kombat II, Supergirl, and Clayface. It debuted in more than 4,000 theaters three weeks ago and is now playing​​​​​​​ in roughly 3,200 locations nationwide. With a terrific 89% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes, the movie has all the makings of a home-video hit. This is the second major adaptation of "The Cat in the Hat," following the infamous 2003 movie starring Mike Myers, which grossed $135 million worldwide against a reported budget of $109 million, and now holds an 11% Rotten Tomatoes score. Amazon is running early Black Friday deals on its Fire TV streaming devices, with the Fire TV Stick HD down to $15.99 and the Fire TV Cube at $89.99, $110 off its current list price. The discounts follow an August price increase across the Fire TV lineup. For more editor-vetted tech deals, check out the rest of our Black Friday coverage.

The newest Fire TV Stick HD is $15.99, down from $39.99. This 2026 version of Amazon's entry-level stick is about 30% slimmer than before and able to run off a TV's USB port. It streams in 1080p with HDR10+ over Wi-Fi 6 and adds Alexa+ for more conversational voice search. That said, with the 4K Select costing $2 more and the new Stick 4K $5 more, the HD makes the most sense for TVs that top out at 1080p. This PCMag review has more on its performance.

Fire TV Stick 4K Select is $17.99, down from $49.99, and brings 4K HDR10+ streaming and Alexa+ to Amazon's lowest-priced 4K stick. It launched in October 2025 as the first Fire TV stick to run Vega OS, and it skips Dolby Vision, Dolby Atmos, and Wi-Fi 6, using Wi-Fi 5 instead.

The latest Fire TV Stick 4K is down to $19.99 from $59.99 and is the version Amazon released in September with a quad-core processor, Wi-Fi 6, and Vega OS. According to Amazon, apps launch over 35% faster than on the previous model, while the ability to draw power directly from your TV's USB port makes setup a little easier. The Fire TV Stick 4K Plus with AI-powered Fire TV search is $29.99, down from $69.99, and is built on the second-generation Fire TV Stick 4K hardware that PCMag reviewed in 2023, now paired with AI-powered search that finds titles by actor, plot, or a remembered quote. It supports Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, which the 4K Select lacks, and it runs Fire OS rather than Vega OS, so sideloading still works.

Fire TV Cube is $89.99, down from $199.99, the largest discount in this roundup and $30 below its 2022 launch price. It's Amazon's fastest streaming device, with an octa-core processor, Wi-Fi 6E, a built-in Ethernet port, and far-field microphones for hands-free Alexa. Its HDMI input and IR blaster also let it connect to and control a cable box. For more on its performance, check out this PCMag review.
